final_assessment:
All 10 findings from the fresh proposal pass resolved, 0 stale, 0 deferred — 8 through the obvious-fix lane and 2 through the decision lane, both ratified by chat directive. Artifacts end valid, fingerprints 10/10 verified, deltas at 10 MODIFIED requirements across 3 capabilities, tasks 22 -> 30.

TWO STRUCTURAL CHANGES came out of the decision lane. F3 added a TENTH requirement: the emptiness refusal lives in judgementOrderingCheck, which orbit-emit-composition's `Write-gate validation via the shared normalizers` governs, and that requirement's prose forbade the engine judging 'whether enough of them were cited'. The reconciliation was cleaner than the finding proposed — the requirement already draws the distinction at edge (a), calling an in-context refusal 'well-formedness of the citation, not the forbidden judgement about whether ENOUGH passes were cited' — so the SHALL-NOT needed no narrowing and edge (d) simply joins (a) and (b), with the boundary stated as exactly ZERO. F5 reordered the engine work around a hazard the preamble had missed: validatePayload refuses unknown keys OUTRIGHT, so removing the payload-table entry before the bodies stop composing the field refuses every emit in the window, and the repo's own comment at emit-composition.ts:179-181 records that exact failure happening once before.

The pattern the fresh pass named — 'a boundary drawn one line short' — held up under the walk and produced a second instance of itself: D-rc04c-6's generalisable lesson was 'a grep finds every mention, and a mention is not a dependency', and its twin, which it did not draw, is that a grep finds every FILE and one site is not the file. That is now recorded in design D3 alongside the corrected four-kind classification.

ONE SEAM-ARISEN OBSERVATION, out of scope and deliberately not fixed: `npm test` shows test/core/source-lint.test.ts failing with ENOENT on orbit/explore/rc04c-retire-gate-overridden/explore.md. It is NOT caused by this walk. The lint enumerates via `git ls-files` — the INDEX, not the worktree — and propose moved explore.md with `mv` without staging the deletion, so the lint reads a path git still tracks. Measured: the ENOENT set is exactly that one file, and the file at its NEW path is untracked and therefore currently invisible to the lint. Both conditions resolve at commit. Two observations worth carrying to the program rather than to this stage: the lint hard-fails (an exception, not a clean finding) on a state that EVERY consume-mode propose creates between the move and the commit, and during that window the moved document is unlinted. That belongs with Q-crc-14, which already records that the lint ships with no trigger.
